title: IELTS Academic 19 - Listening Test 3 - Part 2
transcriptHtml:
LISTENING TRANSCRIPT - PART 2

💡 Audio-Track Sync: Bấm vào bất kỳ câu nào dưới đây để phát audio ngay đúng câu đó!

06:37ANNOUNCER: Part 2. You will hear the organiser of a children's book festival giving some information about it on a local radio programme.
06:48ANNOUNCER: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 16.
07:22ANNOUNCER: Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 16.
07:30PRESENTER: The children's book festival is coming up again soon and here to tell us all about it is the festival's organiser, Jenny Morgan. So tell us what we can expect this year, Jenny.
07:42JENNY: Well, as usual we've got five days of action-packed exciting events for children, with writers coming from all over the country getting involved.
07:54JENNY: Just to give you an idea of what's on offer in the workshops, first of all, there's a very special event called Superheroes. This is a chance for deaf children to share their reading experiences with author Madeleine Gordon, who is herself hearing impaired.
08:12JENNY: 'Just do it' is a practical workshop led by the well-known illustrator Mark Keane. He'll take participants on a magical journey to faraway lands with an opportunity for aspiring actors to do some role play.
08:28JENNY: 'Count on me' is an inspiring and entertaining look at the issues of friendship for 13–14-year-olds. It looks at some of the friendships described in popular books and asks participants to compare these with their own experiences.
08:45JENNY: 'Speak up' is part of a series of workshops on the subject of mental health. This is a creative writing workshop encouraging children to describe situations where young people experience loneliness. A recent survey revealed that children can be lonely even when they're at home with their families.
09:07JENNY: 'Jump for joy', as many of you will know, is the heart-warming, best-selling story by Nina Karan about a young girl's trip to visit her relatives in India. It recently received the gold medal at the Waterford Awards. Nina will get children to celebrate the word 'joy' by writing a poem.
09:29JENNY: 'Sticks and stones' is the beautifully illustrated picture book for young readers about a community who organise an African-Caribbean festival to help local children learn about their Jamaican roots. This will be a musical event where children will have the chance to play steel drums. This is bound to be very popular, so please book as soon as possible.
09:56ANNOUNCER: Before you hear the rest of the programme, you have some time to look at questions 17 to 20.
10:23ANNOUNCER: Now listen and answer questions 17 to 20.
10:30PRESENTER: Thanks Jenny. That all sounds really interesting. I'm just wondering if you have a favourite book you could recommend for our readers?
10:39JENNY: It's hard to choose, but Alive and Kicking is definitely worth mentioning. You won't have heard of the writer as it's her first book – which is really impressive. It's basically the teenage diary of a boy from Somalia who comes to live in the UK. It deals with the serious issue of immigration and all the challenges the boy has to face at school and with the language barrier, etc. Usually, books like this are quite sad, but this one actually made me cry with laughter. On each page, there are simple but hilarious black and white stick drawings of the boy with his friends and teachers. At the end of each diary entry, there are new English words the boy learns each day, which may help develop some children's vocabulary.
11:29PRESENTER: I think my kids would enjoy that. What about any advice for parents on how to encourage their children to read more?
11:37JENNY: Well, this is something I get asked about a lot. There are so many distractions for kids these days that it can be hard to find time for reading. One thing I'd say is to make time to sit down with your child and share books with them. A lot of parents give up reading aloud to their children as soon as they learn to read independently, but this is a mistake. It's good to read more advanced books to them as it helps to develop their vocabulary. If you don't have time for this, then let them listen to audio books. Often, they'll want to read books they've listened to for themselves. I think it's a good idea to make a mental note of the type of books your child is reading – often they just read the same genre all the time, which can get a bit boring. You can introduce new authors and genres to them. Librarians should be able to help you with this.
12:36ANNOUNCER: That is the end of part two. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part two.

groups.title: Questions 11–16
groups.instructions:
What information is given about each of the following festival workshops?
Choose SIX answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–H, next to Questions 11–16.

options.text: will be led by a prize-winning author
is aimed at children with a disability
is aimed at a specific age group
raises awareness of a particular culture

groups.title: Questions 17–18
groups.instructions:
Choose TWO letters, A–E.
Which TWO reasons does the speaker give for recommending Alive and Kicking?

groups.title: Questions 19–20
groups.instructions:
Choose TWO letters, A–E.
Which TWO pieces of advice does the speaker give to parents about reading?

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C (is aimed at children with a disability)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'This is a chance for deaf children... who is herself hearing impaired.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'deaf children / hearing impaired' = children with a disability.
• Đáp án đúng: D (involves a drama activity)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'an opportunity for aspiring actors to do some role play.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'actors to do some role play' = drama activity.
• Đáp án đúng: F (is aimed at a specific age group)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'Count on me is an inspiring and entertaining look at the issues of friendship for 13–14-year-olds.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'for 13–14-year-olds' = a specific age group.
• Đáp án đúng: G (explores an unhappy feeling)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'encouraging children to describe situations where young people experience loneliness.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'experience loneliness' = an unhappy feeling.
• Đáp án đúng: B (will be led by a prize-winning author)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'by Nina Karan... It recently received the gold medal at the Waterford Awards. Nina will get children to...'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'received the gold medal' = prize-winning.
• Đáp án đúng: H (raises awareness of a particular culture)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'an African-Caribbean festival to help local children learn about their Jamaican roots.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'learn about their Jamaican roots' = awareness of a particular culture.

q17.text: Which reason does the speaker give for recommending Alive and Kicking? (First choice)
options: A. It will appeal to both boys and girls.
B. The author is well known.
C. It has colourful illustrations.
D. It is funny.
E. It deals with an important topic.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: D (It is funny)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'this one actually made me cry with laughter... simple but hilarious black and white stick drawings.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'cry with laughter / hilarious' = funny.

q18.text: Which reason does the speaker give for recommending Alive and Kicking? (Second choice)
options: A. It will appeal to both boys and girls.
B. The author is well known.
C. It has colourful illustrations.
D. It is funny.
E. It deals with an important topic.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: E (It deals with an important topic)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'It deals with the serious issue of immigration and all the challenges...'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'serious issue of immigration' = important topic.

q19.text: Which piece of advice does the speaker give to parents about reading? (First choice)
options: A. Encourage children to write down new vocabulary.
B. Allow children to listen to audio books.
C. Get recommendations from librarians.
D. Give children a choice about what they read.
E. Only read aloud to children until they can read independently.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (Allow children to listen to audio books)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'If you don't have time for this, then let them listen to audio books.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'let them listen to audio books' = allow children to listen to audio books.

q20.text: Which piece of advice does the speaker give to parents about reading? (Second choice)
options: A. Encourage children to write down new vocabulary.
B. Allow children to listen to audio books.
C. Get recommendations from librarians.
D. Give children a choice about what they read.
E. Only read aloud to children until they can read independently.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C (Get recommendations from librarians)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'You can introduce new authors and genres to them. Librarians should be able to help you with this.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'Librarians should be able to help' = get recommendations from librarians.
